newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Liberty shines as good Q1 draws foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Liberty shines as good Q1 draws foreigners.

text.p: Shares in Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd rose to a 10-week high on Wednesday, basking in what the company described as "most gratifying" results so far this year.
Buoyed by foreign demand, Liberty added 400 cents by 1020 GMT, raising its share price to 129 rand -- only just shy of its year high of 132 rand. But volumes were eoderate with 117,300 shares traded.
Liberty has been moving steadily higher over the last month from a three-month low of 116.31 rand on April 23.
"We've seen some recent buying into the Liberty stable from off the lows," said James Scott at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

That interest was fuelled, particularly from offshore investors, by the company's statement that its new financial year had got off to a good start with new business figures for the first quarter of 1997 more than 65 percent up on the year-ago level.
"Some of the larger volumes are offshore transactions. We're looking at a Liberty play from an offshore point of view," Scott said.
Last year Liberty's offshore units were a major contributor to the group's earnings, having taken advantage of a buoyant UK economy and the rand's devaluation against sterling.
Based on the group's cheery 1997 outlook, dealers said the share price could strengthen further in the short-term.
"It's got a little more upside potential," a dealer said.
Chairman Donald Gordon told the annual meeting that new business had got off to a comparatively slow start in 1996 but despite this the results for the current year were "most gratifying".
Recurring premium business was 25 percent up on the 1996 comparative level.
Dealers said the market's recent positive feeling towards Liberty was also due to former Johannesburg Stock Exchange executive president Roy Andersen taking the reins as Liberty chief executive.
Liberty said on Wednesday Andersen's appointment would be with immediate effect. He joined the life assurance group as chief executive designate on April 1.
"Everyone here knows Roy and the fact that he's going to be good for Liberty has been in the market since his appointment," said another dealer.

Outgoing chief executive Donald Gordon will stay on as chairman of Liberty Life and all the listed companies within the group. The responsibility for UK operations will, at this stage, remain with Gordon.
